frases.texto: We have reached the great and thrilling final chapter of our unforgettable journey!

frases.texto: Don Quixote will travel back to his village inside a mysterious wooden CAGE, set off once more on new adventures, fly across the skies on the back of a flying horse, and see his loyal squire live his dream of governing an ISLAND!

frases.texto: In this farewell, Sancho Panza will teach us all that true WISDOM does not depend on crowns or riches, but blossoms in the hearts of the simple and the generous.

frases.texto: Chapter 23. The Enchanted Cage. A Journey by Ox Cart
frases.fala: Chapter 23. The Enchanted Cage. A Journey by Ox Cart

frases.texto: To take Don Quixote safely back home without hurting his noble heart, his friends built a big CAGE out of oak slats on top of a cart pulled by two slow and gentle white OXEN.
frases.fala: To take Don Quixote safely back home without hurting his noble heart, his friends built a big cage out of oak slats on top of a cart pulled by two slow and gentle white oxen.

frases.texto: While the gentleman slept, worn out from his battles, they settled him inside with the greatest care.
frases.fala: While the gentleman slept, worn out from his battles, they settled him inside with the greatest care.

frases.texto: When he woke up behind the wooden bars, instead of flying into a rage, Don Quixote gave a calm smile: “I am ENCHANTED by a powerful wizard from the books!” he told his companions serenely.
frases.fala: When he woke up behind the wooden bars, instead of flying into a rage, Don Quixote gave a calm smile: I am enchanted by a powerful wizard from the books! he told his companions serenely.

frases.texto: “Only the most famous knights in history travel in enchanted carriages like this one!”
frases.fala: Only the most famous knights in history travel in enchanted carriages like this one!

frases.texto: And so the procession rolled slowly on across the golden meadows: the cart wheels creaking in steady rhythm, the oxen mooing sweetly in the breeze, Sancho trotting alongside on his faithful donkey, and Don Quixote waving happily from inside his enchanted cell, dreaming of the glorious adventures that lay ahead!
frases.fala: And so the procession rolled slowly on across the golden meadows: the cart wheels creaking in steady rhythm, the oxen mooing sweetly in the breeze, Sancho trotting alongside on his faithful donkey, and Don Quixote waving happily from inside his enchanted cell, dreaming of the glorious adventures that lay ahead!

frases.texto: Chapter 24. Back Home. Hugs in La Mancha
frases.fala: Chapter 24. Back Home. Hugs in La Mancha

frases.texto: At midday on a sunny Sunday, the ox cart rolled into the flowery square of the village in La Mancha, where all the neighbours came running, curious to greet the travellers.
frases.fala: At midday on a sunny Sunday, the ox cart rolled into the flowery square of the village in La Mancha, where all the neighbours came running, curious to greet the travellers.

frases.texto: His loving NIECE Antonia and the devoted housekeeper covered the gentleman with kisses and tears of relief, tucked him into a soft bed and brought him a delicious bowl of piping-hot chicken soup.
frases.fala: His loving niece Antonia and the devoted housekeeper covered the gentleman with kisses and tears of relief, tucked him into a soft bed and brought him a delicious bowl of piping-hot chicken soup.

frases.texto: Sancho hurried off to his humble little white-walled cottage.
frases.fala: Sancho hurried off to his humble little white-walled cottage.

frases.texto: His devoted wife, Teresa Panza, and his little daughter, Sanchica, ran out to hug him.
frases.fala: His devoted wife, Teresa Panza, and his little daughter, Sanchica, ran out to hug him.

frases.texto: “Did you bring gold coins?” asked Teresa.
frases.fala: Did you bring gold coins? asked Teresa.

frases.texto: “Did you bring fine dresses?” asked Sanchica, jumping for joy.
frases.fala: Did you bring fine dresses? asked Sanchica, jumping for joy.

frases.texto: “I brought something far more precious!” cheered Sancho, twirling his daughter round in his arms.
frases.fala: I brought something far more precious! cheered Sancho, twirling his daughter round in his arms.

frases.texto: “I brought unforgettable memories, courage, and the certainty that one day I shall be made governor of a lovely island!”
frases.fala: I brought unforgettable memories, courage, and the certainty that one day I shall be made governor of a lovely island!

frases.texto: Gathered around the table with homemade bread and olives, the FAMILY listened, deeply moved, to the stories of the windmills and the sheep until late into the night.

frases.texto: Chapter 25. Clavileño, the Flying Horse. A Journey through the Sky without Leaving the Ground
frases.fala: Chapter 25. Clavileño, the Flying Horse. A Journey through the Sky without Leaving the Ground

frases.texto: Months later, hearing the call of adventure, which no knight can resist, the two companions set off once more along the roads of the world!
frases.fala: Months later, hearing the call of adventure, which no knight can resist, the two companions set off once more along the roads of the world!

frases.texto: And they had a delightful surprise: their old adventures had been written down and published in a great book, and now the Knight of the Sorrowful Face was famous all over Spain.
frases.fala: And they had a delightful surprise: their old adventures had been written down and published in a great book, and now the Knight of the Sorrowful Face was famous all over Spain.

frases.texto: A rich and noble duke and duchess, who had loved reading the story, welcomed the two friends into their grand palace.
frases.fala: A rich and noble duke and duchess, who had loved reading the story, welcomed the two friends into their grand palace.

frases.texto: There, they put on an unforgettable piece of play-acting: they brought out CLAVILEÑO, an enormous wooden horse with a magic peg in its neck which, they said, had the power to fly above the clouds.

frases.texto: Chapter 26. Advice for a Governor. Sancho Will Govern an Island
frases.fala: Chapter 26. Advice for a Governor. Sancho Will Govern an Island

frases.texto: Carrying on with the game, the noble duke gave Sancho the much-desired governorship of the “Isle of Barataria”, which was really a busy, pretty town out in the countryside.
frases.fala: Carrying on with the game, the noble duke gave Sancho the much-desired governorship of the Isle of Barataria, which was really a busy, pretty town out in the countryside.

frases.texto: On the evening before he left, Don Quixote invited his faithful squire to sit with him on a stone bench in the garden and shared the wisest ADVICE a master can give:
frases.fala: On the evening before he left, Don Quixote invited his faithful squire to sit with him on a stone bench in the garden and shared the wisest advice a master can give:

frases.texto: “Sancho, my brother of the road, never be ashamed of your humble beginnings, and never hide that you are the son of honest farmers.
frases.fala: Sancho, my brother of the road, never be ashamed of your humble beginnings, and never hide that you are the son of honest farmers.

frases.texto: Treat the barefoot townsman and the wealthy lord with the same kindness and care.
frases.fala: Treat the barefoot townsman and the wealthy lord with the same kindness and care.

frases.texto: Always grow your HUMILITY, seek the truth with endless patience, and remember that the noblest JUSTICE is the kind that walks hand in hand with mercy and forgiveness.”
frases.fala: Always grow your humility, seek the truth with endless patience, and remember that the noblest justice is the kind that walks hand in hand with mercy and forgiveness.

frases.texto: Sancho listened to every lesson with his eyes brimming with feeling and respect.
frases.fala: Sancho listened to every lesson with his eyes brimming with feeling and respect.

frases.texto: Deeply moved, he hugged his dear gentleman, promised to keep every word in his heart, and set off to begin governing, trotting proudly along on his beloved donkey.

frases.texto: Chapter 27. The Mystery of the Walking Stick. The Cleverest Judgement
frases.fala: Chapter 27. The Mystery of the Walking Stick. The Cleverest Judgement

frases.texto: On his very first day sitting in the island’s court, Sancho came across a puzzling mystery between two old neighbours.
frases.fala: On his very first day sitting in the island’s court, Sancho came across a puzzling mystery between two old neighbours.

frases.texto: The first one complained: “I lent my friend ten gold COINS and he refuses to give them back!”
frases.fala: The first one complained: I lent my friend ten gold coins and he refuses to give them back!

frases.texto: The second one insisted, with his hand on his heart: “I solemnly swear before this court that I have already put every single coin back into his own hands!”
frases.fala: The second one insisted, with his hand on his heart: I solemnly swear before this court that I have already put every single coin back into his own hands!

frases.texto: Before taking the sacred oath, the second old man politely asked his neighbour to hold his heavy wooden WALKING STICK.
frases.fala: Before taking the sacred oath, the second old man politely asked his neighbour to hold his heavy wooden walking stick.

frases.texto: He swore the oath, took back his stick and was getting ready to leave without a care in the world.

frases.fala: Chapter 28. Sancho Chooses his Donkey. The Freedom of a Simple Man

frases.texto: Sancho governed the town for ten days with wonderful honesty and fairness.
frases.fala: Sancho governed the town for ten days with wonderful honesty and fairness.

frases.texto: But palace life was tiring and stuffy: a strict doctor would not let him eat anything tasty, the endless meetings kept him awake at night, and all the pomp of power stole away his peace.

frases.texto: One fine morning, dressed in his old, simple farmer’s clothes, Sancho walked to the stable, lovingly hugged the neck of his beloved DONKEY and poured out his heart tenderly: “My loyal FRIEND, when I travelled with you, my days were full of peace and joy.

frases.texto: And so, without taking a single coin from the town’s treasure chest, Sancho said goodbye to the island with his head held high: he left with no riches at all, but with his soul overflowing with goodness, dignity and wisdom.
